topFindings: CRITICAL (document-p18): The tracked-change insertion 'formally' is translated as 'unteroffiziell' ('unofficially'). This reverses the meaning of a legal approval statement.
MAJOR (document-p18): <g id="2"> ends with a space and <g id="4"> starts with one ('unteroffiziell </g><x/><g> vierteljährliche'). This produces a double space around the tracked-change marker.
MAJOR terminology (document-p4): 'Workspace' is left in English instead of the required glossary term 'Arbeitsbereich'.

MAJOR mistranslation (footer1-p22): 'Confidential policy summary' becomes 'Zusammenfassung der Vertraulichkeitsrichtlinie' ('summary of the confidentiality policy'), which changes what the footer says.
MAJOR broken spacing/field (footer1-p22): The space after 'Seite' is missing, so the page-number field runs straight into the word ('Seite1').
MINOR (document-p3): 'Grace Periods' is translated as 'Zahlungsfristen' (payment terms), while footnotes-p23 uses 'Nachfrist'. The term is inaccurate and inconsistent.
MINOR (document-p14): The plan name 'Enterprise' is translated as 'Unternehmensarbeitsbereich'. This is inconsistent with 'Starter-Arbeitsbereich'.
MINOR (document-p2): Spaces are moved inside the formatted brand runs ('Northstar ', 'Northstar Pay '), which can carry run formatting onto the whitespace.
MINOR (comments-p21 / header1-p24): The phrasing is awkward ('Zeitplan „erster Werktag“'), 'confirm' is weakened to 'überprüfen', and 'Richtlinien' is plural where the source is singular.
The tracked-change insertion 'formally' is correctly rendered as 'förmlich' and placed in the right position for German verb-final syntax. Tag integrity and spacing are preserved.
All glossary terms (Arbeitsbereich, Rechnung) and DNT brands (Northstar, Northstar Pay, LedgerVault) are handled correctly. The formal 'Sie' register is used throughout.
MINOR (document-p20): One source sentence is split into two. Acceptable, but it departs from the source structure.
MINOR (comments-p21): Adds 'des Abrechnungszeitraums', which is not in the source.
MINOR (document-p12 / document-p17): The phrasing is awkward ('Aktivitäten der letzten 90 Tage durchsuchbar') or wordy ('Änderungen an den rechtlichen Bestimmungen').

results.rationale: System_A has a critical meaning inversion in the legally sensitive tracked-change segment: it renders 'formally' as 'unofficially'. It also breaks the Workspace=Arbeitsbereich glossary rule, mistranslates the confidential footer, and has spacing defects around the tracked-change marker and the page field. System_B is faithful, follows the glossary and DNT list, keeps the formal register, preserves tags and spacing, and places 'förmlich' correctly. Its only issues are minor stylistic liberties.

topFindings: p1: 'Resumen de alta' leaves out 'del paciente' (minor omission; still acceptable for a heading).
Uses formal 'usted' throughout (Lea, No deje, Acuda, Tome, Mídase, Evite, Su cita, lleve) as required.
All required Mexican terms are used: 'tableta', 'jugo de toronja', 'médico tratante', 'presión arterial'.
The DNT brand names CardioPulse and LedgerVault are kept, and all <g> tags are intact.
p13: 'dentro de los 14 días posteriores al alta' keeps the 'within 14 days' meaning.
Wrong register: informal 'tú' in 7 segments (p2 'Lee'; p3 'dejes/te/tu/Acude/sientes'; p8/p11 'Tómate'; p9 'Controla'; p12 'Evita'; p13 'Tu/Trae/tu') where formal 'usted' was required (7 major).

p12: 'zumo de pomelo' is Peninsular Spanish and breaks the required 'jugo de toronja'. This is a drug-food interaction warning, and Mexican patients may not recognize the term, which is a safety risk (major).

p3: 'médico de cabecera' (GP/family doctor) mistranslates 'attending physician'; the required term is 'médico tratante'. This could send patients to the wrong doctor before changing their medication (major).
p3/p9: 'tensión arterial' is Peninsular Spanish; the required term is 'presión arterial' (2 major).
p8/p11: 'comprimido' replaces the required 'tableta' (2 major).
p13: 'programada para dentro de 14 días tras el alta' changes 'within 14 days' to 'in 14 days' (mistranslation, major).
Minor Peninsular wording: 'Medicación' (p3, p4) instead of 'medicamento'; 'te han recetado' uses the Spain-style compound past; 'Trae' is used where 'lleve' is meant.

results.rationale: System_A meets every stated requirement: formal 'usted', Mexican terms (tableta, jugo de toronja, médico tratante, presión arterial), brand names left untranslated, and tags intact. Its only flaw is a minor heading omission. System_B uses informal 'tú' throughout and Peninsular Spanish (tensión arterial, comprimido, zumo de pomelo, médico de cabecera, medicación), which breaks the es-MX glossary. Some of these errors affect safety in a clinical letter: the grapefruit interaction warning and who the patient should consult before stopping blood-pressure medication. It also gets the follow-up timeframe wrong. System_A wins decisively: 99.29 to 47.14.
